overview: Implementation study in three long-term care homes, January to December 2027: monthly interdisciplinary deprescribing rounds with a structured checklist, a named deputy and a protected slot in each home, evaluated with RE-AIM outcomes from round notes, medication administration records and incident reports.
population: All residents of the three homes (168 beds) during 2027, including short-stay residents; the staff who run the rounds.
exposure: Monthly rounds of about one hour: pharmacist (or the named deputy), attending physician, nurse in charge and, when possible, the resident or substitute decision-maker; four to six residents per round, prioritised by number of medicines and time since last review; recommendations recorded in the administration record with an owner and a date.
procedures: Before January, each home names a deputy (a senior nurse trained by the pharmacist) and fixes a monthly slot next to the physician's visit. Round notes use a template with the eight checklist steps. The informatics lead exports administration records monthly; the pharmacist links recommendations to changes within four weeks and to restarts within 30 days. One round per home per quarter is observed with a short fidelity checklist.

outcomes.name: Reach
outcomes.measure: Proportion of residents with at least one round review within six months of admission or of the first round, by home
outcomes.why: Whether rounds touch the residents they are meant for.

outcomes.name: Adoption and maintenance
outcomes.measure: Rounds held out of 12 scheduled per home, including rounds held when the pharmacist was absent
outcomes.why: Sustainability was the failure in the first home.

outcomes.name: Recommendations carried out
outcomes.measure: Proportion of recommendations implemented in the administration record within four weeks
outcomes.why: A recommendation that is not carried out changes nothing for the resident.

outcomes.name: Fidelity
outcomes.measure: Checklist completion index (eight core steps) from round notes, with quarterly observation
outcomes.why: Shows whether goals of care and action owners are recorded.

outcomes.name: Regular medicines per resident
outcomes.measure: Count of regular medicines from the administration record
outcomes.why: The expected direct result of rounds.

outcomes.name: Falls and restarts
outcomes.measure: Falls per 1,000 resident-days from incident reports; proportion of stopped medicines restarted within 30 days
outcomes.why: Deprescribing must not cause harm or reversals.

feasibility: The pharmacist's 0.4 FTE covers one round per home per month plus follow-up; data come from existing records exported by the informatics lead; no forms are added for care staff.
biasMitigation: Outcomes defined from routine records before the first round
Reach reported by home, length of stay and substitute decision-maker participation
Quarterly observation to check documentation-based fidelity
Secular changes in prescribing noted on a timeline of events

biasFlags.label: No comparison group
biasFlags.note: Changes in medicines cannot be attributed to rounds alone; the study does not claim they can.

biasFlags.label: Documentation-based fidelity
biasFlags.note: Undocumented steps are invisible; quarterly observation limits this.

biasFlags.label: Selective prioritisation of residents
biasFlags.note: A fixed prioritisation rule avoids choosing easy reviews.

flags: Three process measures follow RE-AIM; clinical outcomes are secondary or balancing only
parsimony.simplestPath: One primary implementation outcome from routine records, three process measures, one balancing pair.

theoreticalFramework: RE-AIM organises the outcomes; no further framework is added because the study does not test causal mechanisms.
summary: RE-AIM implementation study with reach as the primary outcome, three process measures, medicine count as secondary and falls with restarts as balancing.
